items.notes: Personnel screening/vetting of developers maps directly to Personnel security; the control explicitly distinguishes internal (PS-3) from external developer screening, both within this hub's lifecycle scope.
Governance program for AI security maps to AI management system; siblings cover specific sub-activities like compliance and education.
Fundamentally about poisoning of training data via compromised dataset sources; data supply chain management is a defensible alternative given the URL/hash provenance framing.
Network-layer attack evading IPS/firewall filtering with DoS side effects; defense-in-depth for network attacks fits best, DoS protection is secondary since resource exhaustion is only one outcome.
The control constrains encryption of sensitive data at rest (including models); Protection of technical AI information is defensible since AI models are the named asset.
Exact match: leaks of model artifacts via compromised development environments and repositories.

Attack exploits cleartext HTTP after TLS termination between infrastructure components; inter-component communication encryption fits, though missing authentication of external connections is also implicated.
Covers both direct and indirect prompt injection; direct is the primary framing since the adversary crafts the prompts, with indirect explicitly described as a variant.
Network reconnaissance scan with no dedicated hub; network defense-in-depth (which includes IDS/IPS detection) is the least-bad home.
Covers runtime detection/filtering defenses against prompt injection; testing-against-direct-prompt-injection is defensible but the text is broader than pre-deployment testing.
Encoding-based parser/validation discrepancy attack; uniform encoders/parsers hub addresses exactly this class, with HTTP input whitelisting as an alternative.
Routing/pharming manipulation has no exact hub; name/address resolution integrity is closest for the pharming example, though general traffic redirection is broader.
Unicode encoding bypass of non-Unicode-aware filters is a parser/encoding discrepancy; same family as item 12.
Adversarial training is named explicitly; robust distillation and the evasion-preventing training parent are acceptable.
Rootkit installation is malware on endpoints; the backdoor-detection hub is a near-miss but is scoped to source/dependency analysis rather than runtime malware.
Non-network eavesdropping on conversations has no dedicated hub; physical/environmental protection is the only plausible home.
Input restoration is explicitly named in the AI Input distortion hub description.
Network reconnaissance/probing attack with no dedicated hub; defense-in-depth for network attacks is the closest defensible home.
Rogue location mimicking a legitimate resource origin maps to trusted-origin verification (typosquatting/dependency confusion analog).
Fundamentally about physical/environmental protection policy; policy review hub is a secondary fit since the control also mandates review cycles.
Control covers both direct and indirect prompt injection; chose the direct-injection leaf as primary since the text leads with direct user-prompt manipulation.
Extraction through the query-response interface (inversion, membership inference, model extraction) fits direct runtime model leak best.
Buffer overflow from expanded input; memory-safe function usage is the closest hub since no generic buffer-overflow hub exists.
Attack harvests data leaked during API/event transactions; no good home exists, information-disclosure hub is the weakest-but-defensible fit.
OS fingerprinting probe; no reconnaissance hub in taxonomy, network defense-in-depth is the only plausible placement.
Fundamentally role-specific training; contingency planning hub is acceptable since content is tied to contingency operations.
PII quality operations is explicitly named in the personal data handling management description.
Port scanning attack pattern; no reconnaissance hub exists, network defense-in-depth is the least-bad fit.
Same rationale as other TCP scan items: no dedicated scanning/reconnaissance hub.
DNS-specific availability attack; DoS hub is secondary since the vector is name resolution.
Attack is unauthorized file enumeration/disclosure; directory browsing hub fits best though the control text is broader file access control.
Attack culminates in script execution in victim's browser and cookie theft; fundamentally XSS.
OS fingerprinting via ICMP quoting is technical information disclosure, but the hub is HTTP-specific; no clean home in the taxonomy.
Buffer overflow via conversion routine; memory-safe function use is the closest control home.
Control spans backdoor testing, leakage testing, and drift monitoring; backdoor poisoning validation is the most distinctive element.
Network reconnaissance technique with no dedicated hub; monitoring/detection of network activity is the closest defensible home.
General interaction-frequency limit; request-intensity monitoring fits best, with authentication-specific and automation-abuse hubs as plausible alternatives.
SI-12 is broader than personal data, but retention-driven classification/deletion is the closest hub; the personal-data scoping of 268-272 is a slight mismatch.
LLM02 centers on sensitive data (incl. training data) disclosed through model output; the technical mitigation hub 204-272 is a defensible alternative.
CWE-233 is generic parameter handling; allowlist input validation is the closest general home.
Nested exponential expansion is the decompression-bomb class; general DoS is a secondary fit.
Buffer overflow via binary file content maps to memory-safe function requirements; compile-time hardening is a defensible alternative.
Control also mentions in-context/augmentation data manipulation, hence 217-163 as acceptable.
Malicious payload delivered via seemingly normal files; malware scanning of untrusted files is the closest fit, with file validation and execution blocking as alternatives.
Control is output encoding of model text to prevent injection in downstream consumers; hub 430-722's description (information leakage) does not match despite the name overlap.
Cache poisoning spans DNS/ARP/browser caches; DNS integrity hub is the best available home though the CAPEC is broader.
CWE-1230 is about access control gaps on derived metadata; no dedicated hub exists, sensitive-data identification/policy is the closest fit.
Hardware fault injection to extract keys has no dedicated hub; physical/environmental protection is the least-bad fit, with cryptography as an alternative.
Enforcing one-time actions maps best to business flow sequence enforcement; business logic limits is a defensible alternative.
General TOCTOU race condition; the sensitive-function sibling is acceptable when the check guards a security decision.
Artifact collection spans models, datasets, and telemetry; no single hub covers collection as a staging step, so exfiltration is the closest conceptual home.
Attack on detection tooling has no dedicated hub; monitoring/detection capability is the closest match.
Rainbow table attacks are defeated by salting; the salt-specific sibling is equally defensible.
AI Exchange control on retention limits; training data retention management fits the AI context, though the text is generic enough for the data-scattering and personal-data retention hubs.
Validation of GenAI output against security/content/privacy policy maps to sensitive output handling; conventional injection in output is a narrower alternative.
OS fingerprinting is reconnaissance with no dedicated hub; technical information disclosure is the nearest fit though the description is HTTP-scoped.
Custom development of critical components is fundamentally about not trusting third-party provenance; backdoor checking is a defensible alternative.
Shared high-privilege unlock credentials across parties maps to disallowing shared privileged accounts, though the hardware/firmware flavor is unusual.
Network topology enumeration is reconnaissance with no dedicated hub; network defense-in-depth is the only network-attack hub available.
Unvalidated index/offset is fundamentally input validation; memory-safety and boundary-checking siblings are defensible given buffer overflow consequences.
Mutable boot-measurement registers undermine integrity verification of code artifacts; trusted-source integrity checks is a defensible alternative.
Manipulation/disinformation attacks prompt the model to produce wrong outputs; broader than direct prompt injection, so the inference-time behaviour-integrity parent fits best.
Cross-field consistency validation of structured input maps to schema enforcement on structured data.
Memory-exhaustion DoS via SOAP array declaration; fundamentally a resource-exhaustion attack, with XML schema enforcement as a secondary mitigation.
Network reconnaissance pattern with no dedicated hub; layered network defense/detection is the least-bad fit.
Covers both model artifact scanning and training-data hash verification; model supply chain is the dominant theme.
ICMP reconnaissance; taxonomy lacks a recon hub, network defense-in-depth is the closest defensible home.
Attack includes deletion and forgery, broader than log injection alone, so the log-integrity parent is primary.
Core dump exposure is sensitive data recoverable from memory; zeroization is the closest control, though not a perfect fit.
General race-condition exploitation across resources; the general thread-safety hub fits better than the security-critical-function sibling.
Functional model copy reconstructed from repeated queries matches model exfiltration's description; runtime leak sibling is a defensible alternative.
Encoding-discrepancy abuse to bypass URL validation; uniform encoder/parser enforcement addresses exactly this parser-differential class.
Nested-payload parser resource exhaustion causing DoS; schema enforcement on XML is a secondary mitigation.
Primarily training/fine-tuning data poisoning; malicious pickled models noted in passing would be supply-chain poisoning.
Server trusting a spoofed client is fundamentally failure to authenticate external connections.
Account/permission enumeration has no dedicated hub; discovery-attack prevention is the closest defensible fit.
Control spans training-time robustness techniques; adversarial training hub is the closest leaf, but the broader evasion-preventing training parent also fits.
Reconnaissance attack pattern with no dedicated hub; network defense-in-depth/detection hub is the least-bad fit.
Fundamentally about restricting an AI agent's tool permissions when processing untrusted data; privilege minimization fits best, prompt injection I/O handling is a defensible alternative.
Attack on cellular/wireless encryption; wireless link protection is closest, though the taxonomy has no cryptanalysis attack hub.
Randomized smoothing is explicitly named in the AI Input distortion hub description.
Weakness in privilege assignment/tracking maps to least privilege enforcement; the minimize-permissions parent is also defensible.
Bluetooth key negotiation attack is a wireless link threat; cryptography hub is a secondary fit for the key/entropy aspect.
Preventing memorization of training samples primarily mitigates direct data disclosure in model output; inference-based extraction hubs are secondary.
Privilege abuse is an authorization failure; the strong authorization checking parent has no description, so leaf choices are approximate.
Multi-sensor redundancy against physical/evasion attacks maps loosely to ensemble model robustness; no dedicated physical-attack hub exists.
Spoofed automated update delivery is squarely secure auto-update territory.
AI-specific supply chain management hub matches directly; conventional and sub-asset hubs are acceptable alternates.
OS fingerprinting is reconnaissance; no dedicated hub, so network attack detection/response is the least-bad fit.
Exact match to the Train data distortion hub.
Buffer overflow via symlink is a memory-safety weakness; memory-safe functions hub fits, compile-time hardening is secondary.
Forced use of corrupted files spans validation, fail-secure, and untrusted file storage; validation of untrusted file data is the most defensible single choice.
Guidelines steering model behavior toward desired outputs align with GenAI model alignment; prompt segregation is a plausible alternative reading.
Broad access control weakness; the strong authorization checking parent is the best umbrella, with least-privilege and server-side enforcement as defensible leaves.
Exact match to the Model output contains conventional injection hub.
Dictionary attack is credential guessing; rate limiting/lockout controls fit best, though the taxonomy has no dedicated password-guessing hub.
Host-discovery scanning has no dedicated hub; layered network detection/response is the closest defensible home.
TCP window scanning is network reconnaissance; no dedicated hub exists.
Ajax footprinting is enumeration/recon with no dedicated hub; network defense-in-depth with detection is the closest fit.
Stealth port scanning; no dedicated hub, layered network defense is closest.
Fingerprinting relies on disclosure of technical version details; the HTTP information-disclosure hub is the best available home.
Economy-of-mechanism is a design/architecture principle; the Architecture hub is the only structural-design home.
Buffer overflow via oversized tag/variable strings; memory-safe function use is the primary mitigation, compile-time hardening a secondary.
Cryptographic verification of AI model artifacts maps to model supply chain integrity verification.
W^X/DEP hardware exclusivity aligns with compile/build-time executable hardening (DEP, ASLR) hub.
Format/encoding manipulation to bypass validation; allowlist input validation is primary, uniform encoders/parsers and schema enforcement are defensible alternates.
RAG poisoning is manipulation of augmentation/retrieval data sources; indirect prompt injection is a secondary aspect when the poisoned content contains injections.
Sensitive data persisted in browser cookies maps to avoiding sensitive data in client browser storage; secure cookie storage of session tokens is the near-miss sibling.
DP as a training-data transformation is obfuscation; DP as reducing data footprint (data minimization) is a defensible alternative.
Device lock on inactivity is functionally a session timeout mechanism.
Session hijacking is fundamentally a session integrity threat; resist stolen credentials is a defensible alternative since hijacked sessions are abused credentials.
Reconnaissance via process enumeration has no dedicated hub; the parent prevent-security-disclosure hub is the least bad fit.
Encoding-based validation bypass is fundamentally a parser/encoder discrepancy problem; general unstructured data sanitization is secondary.
Adversary discovery of sensitive data on local systems maps best to the defensive concept of identifying sensitive data and subjecting it to policy; no dedicated hub exists.
Service modification is an OS-level configuration attack; OS security (service restrictions) fits better than change management since this is adversarial, not procedural.
Survey section spanning membership inference, inversion, and extraction; the parent inference-based training data confidentiality hub is the best single home.
Generic white-box reverse engineering of software has no dedicated hub; only the broad prevent-security-disclosure parent is defensible.
Spans direct model manipulation via malicious updates and supply-chain scenarios; the model poisoning parent hub avoids over-committing to one sibling.
Fundamentally supply chain risk management policy; review-of-security-policies is a secondary fit given the review/update requirements.
Same reconnaissance/data-discovery pattern as local system collection; identifying and policy-binding sensitive data is the closest defensive concept.
Data remanence from incomplete deletion maps to limiting sensitive data retention/scattering; retention-based deletion classification is a defensible alternative.
Label flipping and crafted training samples are textbook data poisoning of training datasets.
Explicitly described as a CSRF variant riding the victim's session, though standard CSRF protections may not fully apply since no state change occurs.
Guardrails are runtime filtering/moderation controls; automated AI oversight fits best, though prompt-injection I/O handling is a plausible alternative given the jailbreak/injection emphasis.
OS-created temporary screenshots of sensitive data fit cached/temporary sensitive data lifecycle controls; no dedicated hub exists for this attack.
AI Exchange control targeting resource-exhaustion inputs at inference; generic max input size validation is a defensible alternative.
AI BOM spans model and dataset provenance; model supply chain management is the closest single home.
SCRM planning is governance-level supply chain risk management; the intermediate supply chain management hub is the best fit.
LLM moderator is a runtime detection/filtering defense against indirect prompt injection; automated oversight is a near-equal alternative.
Entry is fundamentally about supply-chain compromise of third-party models via tampering/poisoning; the management-side hub 852-770 is a defensible alternative.
Hardware debug chaining flaw is a design/architecture boundary error; no dedicated hub covers hardware debug access.
Identifier lifecycle management sits under secure user management; no dedicated identifier-management hub exists.
Encoding-based validation bypass is fundamentally an injection/validation attack; uniform encoder enforcement is a control-side alternative.
Broad poisoning technique spanning weight manipulation and poisoned training data; the parent AI model poisoning hub fits best.
